subject: Security exhibit — proposed breach-specific liability sublimit
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-corp.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc:

Subject: Security exhibit — proposed breach-specific liability sublimit

Alex / legal team — attaching an initial draft of a security exhibit that calls out a breach-specific liability sublimit and a few carve-outs tied to the SOC2 controls & incident response obligations. High level: we want to keep overall MSA cap intact but create a narrowly tailored sublimit for incidents involving customer data to give Acme more predictability while protecting Redwood from open-ended exposure.

Key proposal (excerpt):
"For any Security Incident involving Customer Data, the parties agree that Redwood's aggregate liability for all such incidents shall not exceed the lesser of (i) $1,000,000 USD, or (ii) three (3) times the average monthly committed fees paid by Customer to Redwood during the twelve (12) months preceding the incident. This amount shall be in addition to the general liability cap set forth in the MSA. This sublimit applies to direct damages only and excludes consequential, punitive, and special damages. Notwithstanding the foregoing, liability for gross negligence or willful misconduct shall not be limited to the extent not permitted by applicable law"

Open items we want help on from Acme legal:
- Are you comfortable with the formula tie to monthly committed fees (gives elasticity)?
- Do you need regulatory fines & penalties expressly carved out or treated as consequential?
- Is the "direct damages only" drafting sufficient for you to feel comfortable excluding consequential losses?
- Acceptable to trigger the sublimit only where Redwood is the proximate cause of the incident (i.e., excluding upstream customer misconfigurations)?

Attachment: security-exhibit-draft-v1.docx (redline-ready).

Call to action: If this looks directionally okay, can we get proposed redlines back by Friday so we can include in the order form sync next week?

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Security exhibit — proposed breach-specific liability sublimit

Jonas — quick internal note before we send back to Acme. I reviewed the draft and flagged a few concerns in the attached PDF. Summary:
- $1M floor vs. formula: $1M cap might be low relative to mid-market deals if committed spend ramp is slow; tying to "lesser of $1M or 3x monthly committed fees" could accidentally reduce exposure below customer expectation. Consider flipping to "greater of $1M or 3x monthly committed fees" or simply a fixed dollar band by deal tier.
- Regulatory fines: these are often statutory and outside indemnity; Acme will likely push to have fines covered under the sublimit or specifically excluded. We should propose language that treats fines as "covered only to the extent insured or direct awarded damages" — otherwise reject.
- Consequential vs. reliance damages: "direct damages only" is fine but we should add a definition of "direct damages" for clarity (e.g., not including lost profits, business interruption).
- Allocation for third-party breach costs (forensic, notice, credit monitoring): propose a carve-out bucket (e.g., up to $250k outside the sublimit) but only if Acme accepts a higher cap.

I attached redlined-exhibit-laura-comments.pdf with inline suggestions. My recommendation: hold the current approach as a negotiation starter, but be prepared with alternative banding by ARR tier. I'll be available to jump on a call with Acme counsel if needed.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-corp.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:26:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — proposed breach-specific liability sublimit

Hi Jonas / Laura — thanks for the draft and the transparency. A few points from Acme legal:
- Trigger threshold: Acme will want the sublimit to apply to any incident that results in unauthorized access, disclosure, or exfiltration of Customer Data, regardless of the cause. Please confirm you will accept that trigger language.
- Regulatory fines & statutory penalties: given our regulatory footprint, we need explicit language allowing recovery of regulatory fines (or at least carving them out from "consequential damages") where not otherwise prohibited by law.
- Third-party remediation costs: we typically expect reasonable remediation costs (forensic, notifications, call center) to be recoverable outside of a punitive cap; otherwise we may under-allocate budget for incident response.
- Carve-outs we cannot accept: broad "direct damages only" without definition — this creates ambiguity around lost business and downstream partner claims.

Attached is a short counterproposal for consideration: acme-counterproposal.docx.

Can we set a short working session tomorrow morning EST to align? Procurement is looping in procurement@acme-corp.com to confirm commercial impact.

Best,
Alex Turner
Sr. Counsel — Enterprise Agreements | Acme Corp
Alex.Turner@acme-corp.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-corp.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — proposed breach-specific liability sublimit

Alex — appreciate the counterpoints, that's helpful. Quick responses and a proposed compromise to move negotiations forward: 
- Trigger: acceptable to adopt your proposed trigger language (unauthorized access, disclosure or exfiltration of Customer Data) provided we add a proximate-cause qualifier that excludes incidents caused solely by customer's negligent misconfiguration or malicious insider actions.
- Regulatory fines: we cannot broadly assume unlimited regulatory fines. Compromise: fines to be recoverable only to the extent (i) awarded by a final binding order against Redwood, and (ii) not covered by applicable insurance. Alternatively, we can agree to treat reasonable regulatory penalties as part of the sublimit but increase the dollar cap.
- Remediation costs: we are open to a dedicated remediation bucket for reasonable forensic and notification costs (proposed $250,000) outside the sublimit if Acme accepts an increased sublimit to $2,000,000 or a formula of 6x monthly committed fees.
- Definition: agree to include clear definitions for "direct damages" and illustrative examples for excluded consequential damages.

Next steps: Laura / Marissa — can you confirm whether the remediation bucket and $2M counter (or 6x monthly) is acceptable from a legal/ops perspective? If yes, I'll propose that compromise to Acme and request their redlines.

Attachment: none (updated language will follow in a redline).

Jonas
